summary: ClauseClock Stage 2 (renewal_notice extraction) verified end-to-end against real Claude Sonnet 4.6 via Emergent. Stage 1 gate regression: 7/7 PASS (docx, twocol pdf, 40-page pdf, appendix, tables, scanned guardrail, hard delete). Stage 2 backend: 9/9 PASS in ~42s covering happy path, annual-value provenance (extracted + user-entered not overwritten), missing-effective-date needs_review, missing-notice-days needs_review, no-renewal-language no-finding, manual/non-renewing action_required=false, source verbatim integrity vs raw_text, and cross-user isolation (404). Frontend E2E PASS: login, /app/contracts/{id}, click analyze-button, hero date JAN 14 + 147 days remaining + confidence 'high', key facts (next_renewal March 15 2027, notice_period 60 days, notice_method 'certified mail, return receipt requested', notice_recipient 'General Counsel'), contract value $48,000, clause drawer opens and shows clause-renewal_term + clause-notice_period grouped with server-resolved location. Needs-review scenario: hero-date absent, finding-needs-review shows 'NEEDS REVIEW'. Deterministic date math verified (deadline = renewal - 60 days). All model source quotes verbatim-present in the resolved document's raw_text; server-resolved document_id, integer char_offset, and location on every source. No Stage 3+ behaviour exercised.
critical_code_review_comments: analysis.compute_dates uses np.busday_offset with roll='backward'. That’s correct for computing an on-or-before business-day deadline, but note the resulting deadline is always <= renewal-nmin calendar days; that behaviour is fine given the current spec which also flags business-day without definition as needs_review, but worth an inline comment so future contributors don’t mistake it for a calendar-day path.

analysis._sub_days returns numpy.datetime64 -> date via astype in the business branch and datetime.date - timedelta in the calendar branch. The numpy path can silently return an ndarray-scalar; a wrapper `.item()` (or a plain isoformat cast right there) would make the type contract explicit.

server.analyze_contract times out at the default httpx boundary in dev if Claude stalls; consider surfacing an application-level 504/timeout with a stable message so the UI can distinguish 'still working' from 'analysis failed' rather than falling through the generic 'Analysis failed. Try again.'

server.list_findings does not filter by finding.type, so as later stages add types they’ll be commingled with renewal_notice on the ContractDetail page; either scope by type or have the FE filter for renewal_notice explicitly (the FE currently maps all findings straight to FindingCard which is hard-coded to the renewal_notice shape).

llm._parse_json only handles single-value JSON. If a future prompt yields a JSON array of candidates it will match the first bracketed group; low priority given current prompts, but tighten with a strict schema validator (pydantic) at the boundary.

backend/pytest.ini forces `-n 2 --dist loadscope`. Stage 2 uses a module-scoped `pytest.happy_cid` bridge between classes; loadscope keeps them on one worker, but a future contributor adding a new class in this module could accidentally end up on a different worker if class-scoped is applied. Non-blocking (all 9 passed as class-per-scenario).
seed_data_creation: None persisted. Every TEST_stage2_* contract created during Stage 2 runs is hard-deleted by fixture teardown; the E2E happy + noeff contracts are deleted at the end of the playwright run. UserB (stage2-userb-<ts>@clauseclock.app) is created for isolation only and leaves an empty account behind — inert (no contracts).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run Stage 2 with:  python -m pytest /app/backend/tests/test_clauseclock_stage2.py -v -o addopts='' --tb=short  (needs to bypass the project-level xdist addopts). Real Claude call, allow up to ~90s per /analyze; the module runs in ~45s total. Stage 1 regression: python -m pytest /app/backend/tests/test_clauseclock_gate.py -v -o addopts=''  (same reason). Frontend E2E credentials: seeded test user. Reportlab is installed and used to fabricate the test PDFs inline. Class TestAnnualValueProvenance.test_extracted_value_provenance intentionally pytest.skip()s if the model happens not to emit a validated `value` source on that run — this tolerates reasonable model variance without weakening the assertion when the source IS emitted.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. Stage 2 pipeline behaves as specified: (a) validated sources actually appear verbatim (whitespace-normalized) in the resolved document's raw_text; (b) required-purpose gating (renewal_term AND notice_period) enforces needs_review when a required validated source is absent; (c) missing effective_date -> needs_review with no exposed deadline; (d) date math is deterministic (deadline = renewal - notice_days); (e) no unproven $ figure is written to the contract (user_entered is preserved; extracted provenance carries quote/doc_id/location/char_offset); (f) cross-user isolation returns 404 on GET/analyze/findings for another user's contract.
